key_insight: Holomorphic networks enforce the 2D Laplace equation by construction, while boundary-specific singular enrichment improves accuracy near singularities.
engineering_relevance: For 2D Laplace simulations with corner or boundary-condition singularities, analytical structure enables boundary-only training instead of PDE-residual optimization.
method: Compare hybrid harmonic-neural and holomorphic models with PINN baselines.
Enrich the holomorphic model with singular functions matched to junction angles and boundary conditions.
Benchmark against least-squares fits of singular terms and richer classical harmonic bases.
evidence_signal: Across six singular benchmarks, the enriched model leads the compared neural models; on Motz’s problem and the cracked beam, its neural core reduces leading singular-coefficient relative error from about 10⁻² to 10⁻⁶ versus a four-term least-squares fit.
watch_item: Four closed-form benchmarks lie entirely in the enrichment span, and richer classical least-squares bases outperform the network, limiting claims of a neural advantage.
paper_title: Beyond PINNs: Boundary-Enriched Holomorphic Networks for Laplace Problems
